what: Levi Strauss makes jeans. It owns the Levi's brand and the Beyond Yoga activewear label, and has been shifting from selling through other retailers to selling directly in its own stores and website.
customers: Shoppers worldwide, increasingly through Levi's own stores and site rather than department stores.
money: the United States, Canada and Latin America
China, India, Japan and the rest of Asia
moat: A brand with 170 years of recognition in a category where the name on the label is most of the purchase decision, and which can be sold at full price in its own stores.
risks: Denim is fashion-cyclical and a shift away from the current fit cycle would hurt
Wholesale department store customers in America keep shrinking
opportunities: 15.7 times earnings with a 9.2% net margin and $643M of free cash flow
Direct-to-consumer sales now earn the full retail margin instead of sharing it with wholesalers
Analysts see about 14% upside, and the women's and tops ranges are growing faster than men's jeans
watch: Direct-to-consumer revenue share and the gross margin.
